text: They who say that no choice ought to be made, say in effect, that no limit whatsoever ought to be imposed upon the liberty of the press. The one of these propositions is involved in the other. To impose any restraint upon the liberty of the press, is undoubtedly to make a choice. If the restraints is imposed by the movement, it is the movement has the choice after the public mind. If any government chooses the directors of the public mind, that government is depicted.
